title: NECO Financial Accounting Part 1: Foundations, Final Accounts & Records - Financial Accounting - Provision for doubtful debts
exam: NECO Financial Accounting Part 1: Foundations, Final Accounts & Records
subject: Financial Accounting

questions.q: A business has Trade Debtors of ₦40,000 at the end of the year. A specific bad debt of ₦2,000 is discovered and must be written off. The business maintains a provision for doubtful debts at 5% of outstanding debtors. What is the amount of the provision for doubtful debts to be carried forward?
questions.explain:
Before calculating the provision for doubtful debts, all known bad debts must first be deducted from the gross debtors balance. 

1. **Net Debtors:** $\text{₦}40,000 - \text{₦}2,000 = \text{₦}38,000$
2. **Required Provision:** $5\% \times \text{₦}38,000 = \text{₦}1,900$

Therefore, the provision for doubtful debts is **₦1,900**.

questions.q: At the beginning of the year, the Provision for Doubtful Debts account had a credit balance of ₦1,500. At year-end, the required provision is calculated to be ₦1,200. How is this adjustment treated in the Profit and Loss Account?
options: Credited with ₦300 as a gain (reduction in provision)
questions.explain:
When the required provision at the end of the year (₦1,200) is **less than** the existing old provision (₦1,500), there is a **decrease in the provision**.

$$\text{Decrease} = \text{₦}1,500 - \text{₦}1,200 = \text{₦}300$$

A decrease in provision means the business anticipates fewer losses than before. This ₦300 difference is treated as a gain/income and is **credited** to the Profit and Loss Account.
